title: Chromate-Free Surface Protection Scheme for Lower Shell Repair Areas
abstract: A chromate-free protection scheme qualified for repair areas on the lower fuselage shell, replacing the chromated primer that regulation will withdraw and that operators can no longer buy in several jurisdictions.

sections.reason: Hexavalent chromium primers are restricted under European chemicals regulation and several of our operators can no longer obtain them at all, which leaves a repair station able to do the structural work but not able to protect it to the approved scheme. The interim answer, a chromated primer under a derogation, expires and cannot be extended. Twenty-two operators asked for a qualified alternative in the two years to 2024, and three of them were carrying open repairs with a temporary protection because of it.
sections.description: The scheme replaces the chromated etch primer with a sol-gel surface preparation followed by a chromate-free epoxy primer, qualified for the aluminium alloys used in the lower shell and for the titanium splice plates used in repair. The splice plate D5120114264366 and its left-hand equivalent D5120115552469 are re-identified because their supplied protection changes, and the swaged collar LN40979-37 and the protective sleeve AGS443655K5 are re-qualified against the new primer for galvanic compatibility. Surface preparation is by abrasion and solvent wipe rather than by chemical conversion, which removes the tank process from the repair station entirely. The scheme is qualified for the belly fairing areas in zones 181, 183 and 191, which is where most lower shell repair work is done. Detail is on drawing D51201100884.
sections.effects: No mass change: the coating weights are the same to within measurement error. No electrical effect except at bonded joints, where the new primer has a higher resistivity and must be removed locally at every bonding land, which is a change to the repair drawing rather than to the scheme. Fully interchangeable at the structure level; a repair may be done to either scheme and the two may sit side by side. Salt spray performance is equivalent and filiform corrosion performance is better. Repair manual content changes across the lower shell chapters.
sections.embodiment_note: This is a process standard rather than a hardware change, so there is no production cut-in and no retrofit bulletin. It becomes available to a repair station on the date the manual revision is issued. Design is frozen pending the agency finding on the bonded joint resistivity.

type_data.production_impact: None; process standard for repair stations
